name: Meshullam
overview: Meshullam was a male descendant of Bani mentioned in the book of Ezra. His unique distinction in Scripture is that he was among those who had married a foreign wife, a matter addressed in Ezra 10:29. No specific tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshullam means 'restitution' in Hebrew. It is a proper name and was not given directly by God. This meaning may reflect themes of restoration or reconciliation, though the text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Meshullam as a descendant of Bani. Beyond this lineage, no other family relationships are recorded for him apart from his foreign marriage noted in Ezra 10:29.
scriptureSignificance: Meshullam's significance lies in his inclusion among those who had intermarried with foreign women during the post-exilic period, a situation that Ezra addresses as needing correction to maintain covenantal purity. His mention highlights the challenges faced by the returning Israelites in adhering to God's commands and preserving their identity. This underscores the broader biblical theme of faithfulness to God's covenant community.
